stories.headline: Tesla showcases Gen 3 Optimus humanoid robot at AWE 2026 in Shanghai

key_facts.fact: Tesla showcased its upcoming third-generation Optimus humanoid robot at the 2026 Appliance & Electronics World Expo (AWE 2026), which opened March 12 in Shanghai. On-site staff said mass production is scheduled to begin by end of 2026.
key_facts.excerpt: Tesla showcased its upcoming third-generation humanoid robot at the 2026 Appliance & Electronics World Expo (AWE 2026), which opened Thursday in Shanghai. This will be the US electric vehicle (EV) maker's first mass-produced version humanoid robot, with production scheduled to start by the end of 2026.

key_facts.fact: Tesla's long-term planned production capacity for Optimus is 1 million units per year, with its Fremont Factory initial line targeting that volume and Gigafactory Texas expected to produce up to 10 million units per year.
key_facts.excerpt: Tesla previously indicated that it plans to manufacture its humanoid robots at scale once production begins, with its initial production line in the Fremont Factory reaching up to 1 million units annually. An Optimus production line at Gigafactory Texas is expected to produce 10 million units per year.

key_facts.fact: The robot demonstrated highly detailed, human-like hands with finger proportions closely resembling those of a human, able to form a heart shape by precisely touching fingers and thumbs together. Robotic hands are considered one of the hardest engineering challenges in humanoid robotics.
key_facts.excerpt: Tesla China previously shared a teaser image on Weibo showing a pair of highly detailed robotic hands believed to belong to Optimus. The image suggests a design with finger proportions and structures that closely resemble those of a human hand.

key_facts.fact: Elon Musk said in an interview with entrepreneur Peter Diamandis that the Optimus Gen 3 will be the 'most advanced' robot in the world, stating 'Nothing's even close.'
key_facts.excerpt: Elon Musk said that Tesla Inc.'s third-generation Optimus Humanoid robot will be the most advanced robot ever.

stories.headline: Rivian CEO's Mind Robotics raises $500M at $2B valuation for AI-powered factory robots

key_facts.fact: Mind Robotics announced a $500 million Series A round co-led by Accel and Andreessen Horowitz, following a $115 million seed round led by Eclipse Capital in late 2025. Accel partner Sameer Gandhi will join the board.
key_facts.excerpt: Mind Robotics today announced a $500 million Series A round, co-led by Accel and Andreessen Horowitz... This $500 million financing, which is expected to close later this month, follows a seed financing of $115 million led by Eclipse Capital in late 2025.

key_facts.fact: The round values Mind Robotics at $2 billion, making it the largest early-stage investment the robotics industry has ever seen.
key_facts.excerpt: Accel and Andreessen Horowitz led the charge, pushing the company's value up to $2 billion. That's the largest early-stage investment robotics has ever seen.

key_facts.fact: Founded in 2025 by Rivian CEO RJ Scaringe, Mind Robotics is building a full-stack industrial robotics platform for dexterous, variable, and reasoning-intensive factory tasks. Rivian is both partner and major shareholder, providing manufacturing data for model training.
key_facts.excerpt: Rivian Automotive Inc. founder and Chief Executive RJ Scaringe's startup Mind Robotics said today it has raised $500 million in funding at a $2 billion valuation... Mind Robotics is extremely ambitious and intends to build a full-stack robotics platform that incorporates multi-purpose robots plus the foundation models required to make them intelligent and autonomous.

key_facts.fact: The company targets factory tasks that require human-like dexterity and physical reasoning, which current industrial automation cannot handle. Rivian's factories serve as the launch environment for deployment at scale.
key_facts.excerpt: Mind Robotics is building the world's leading industrial robotics platform, capable of deploying AI-enabled robotic systems for dexterous, variable, and reasoning-intensive tasks in factory environments.

stories.headline: Household robot startup Sunday raises $165M Series B at $1.15B unicorn valuation

key_facts.fact: Sunday raised $165 million in a Series B round at a $1.15 billion valuation, led by Coatue Management with Thomas Laffont joining the board. Investors include Bain Capital Ventures, Fidelity, Tiger Global, Benchmark, Conviction, and Xtal Ventures.
key_facts.excerpt: Sunday, the company building helpful home robots, announced it has raised an oversubscribed $165 million Series B funding round at a $1.15 billion valuation. The round was led by Coatue, with Thomas Laffont joining the board.

key_facts.fact: Founded by Tony Zhao and Cheng Chi, Sunday is building a humanoid robot called Memo designed for household tasks like clearing dinner tables, doing laundry, and loading dishwashers. The company plans to deploy its first autonomous robots by Thanksgiving 2026.
key_facts.excerpt: Sunday moves to focus entirely on real-world deployment of its robot, Memo... deploying autonomous object manipulation in a real-world home environment has never been achieved. Sunday plans to break that cycle with their upcoming Beta taking on time-intensive household chores.

key_facts.fact: Sunday owns the full stack from hardware design and manufacturing to its proprietary Skill Capture Glove for data collection, enabling what it calls the industry's fastest model iteration loop. The team includes 70+ engineers from Stanford, Tesla, DeepMind, Waymo, Meta, OpenAI, and Apple.
key_facts.excerpt: Sunday is uniquely positioned to solve general autonomy through the industry's fastest model iteration loop. By owning the full stack, from hardware design and manufacturing to the proprietary Skill Capture Glove, Sunday moves from data collection to model training and evaluation at record speeds.

key_facts.fact: The company emerged from stealth in late 2025 and already has over 1,000 people on its waitlist. It has tripled its engineering staff and quadrupled its research team.
key_facts.excerpt: The company emerged from stealth late last year and already has 1,000 people on its waitlist, Bloomberg reports.

stories.headline: China ends month-long launch hiatus with double mission: Guowang internet and Shiyan-30 test satellites

key_facts.fact: China resumed orbital launches on March 12 after a month-long hiatus with a Long March 8A lifting off from Hainan at 19:48 UTC, carrying the 20th batch of Guowang LEO internet constellation satellites. CASC announced launch success about two hours later.
key_facts.excerpt: The resumption came on Thursday, with a Long March 8A lifting off from Hainan commercial launch center at 2:48 p.m. Eastern, March 12 (1948 UTC). The China Aerospace Science and Technology Corporation (CASC) announced launch success around two hours after liftoff.

key_facts.fact: Less than three hours later, a Long March 2D launched from Xichang at 22:33 UTC on March 12, delivering two Shiyan-30 Earth observation technology test satellites (03 and 04) to low Earth orbit. These were the 631st and 632nd Long March missions.
key_facts.excerpt: A Long March 2D blasted off from Launch Complex 3 at 06:33 am China Standard Time on March 13th (22:33 pm Universal Coordinated Time on March 12th) and flew into low Earth orbit, delivering a pair of satellites.

key_facts.fact: The Guowang constellation now has around 163 operational satellites, with targets of 400 satellites by 2027 and a full constellation of 13,000 satellites. Long March 8A launches typically carry nine Guowang satellites.
key_facts.excerpt: Around 163 operational Guowang satellites currently orbit, with targets of 400 satellites by 2027. The full constellation is designed to include 13,000 satellites.

key_facts.fact: China had not launched since February 12. The extended pause was attributed to the Chinese New Year holiday, annual political sessions in Beijing, and a Long March 3B failure in January.
key_facts.excerpt: The country had not conducted a launch since Feb. 12... ahead of a break for the Chinese New Year holiday. China's annual political sessions in Beijing and a failure of a Long March 3B launch in January may also have contributed to the extended pause.

key_facts.fact: The Shiyan-30 03 and 04 satellites, developed by the Shanghai Academy of Spaceflight Technology, are for experimental verification of Earth observation technologies, following on from the first pair launched in September 2025.
key_facts.excerpt: The test satellites, Shiyan-30 03 and 04, were launched at 6:33 a.m. (Beijing Time) aboard a Long March-2D carrier rocket and entered the preset orbit successfully. The satellites will be mainly used for experimental verification of Earth observation technologies.

stories.headline: Marvell launches four 3nm 1.6T optical DSP chips for AI data center connectivity

key_facts.fact: Marvell introduced four new 3nm 1.6T optical DSP products for AI data centers: Ara T (first 8x200G transmit-retimed optics DSP), Ara X (first 1.6T DSP with advanced link reliability), Petra (first 3nm 8x100G to 4x200G gearbox), and Aquila M (first O-band coherent-lite DSP with integrated MACsec security).
key_facts.excerpt: Marvell Technology, Inc. announced the expansion of its 1.6T portfolio with four industry-first 3nm optical DSP products: Ara T, Ara X, Petra, and Aquila M.

key_facts.fact: The products target scale-up, scale-out, and scale-across AI infrastructure deployments at hyperscale data centers requiring 1.6T pluggable connectivity, building on Marvell's 3nm Ara platform that entered mass volume production for hyperscalers in 2025.
key_facts.excerpt: Solutions target scale-up, scale-out and scale-across AI infrastructure deployments at hyperscale data centers requiring 1.6T pluggable connectivity.

key_facts.fact: Sampling to customers begins in Q1 2026, with a showcase planned at OFC 2026 (March 15-19 in Los Angeles). The products represent Marvell's progression from 5nm 200G/lane DSPs (2023) through the 3nm Ara platform (2024-2025).
key_facts.excerpt: Sampling to customers begins Q1 2026; showcase at OFC 2026 (March 15-19, Los Angeles).

sources.title: Marvell Ushers In the 1.6T Era with Expanded Optical DSP Platform Portfolio, Redefining AI Data Center End-to-End Connectivity

stories.headline: UMC and HyperLight partner to mass-produce TFLN photonics chiplets for 1.6T data centers

key_facts.fact: UMC, HyperLight, and UMC's subsidiary Wavetek announced a strategic collaboration to mass-produce HyperLight's thin-film lithium niobate (TFLN) chiplet platform on 6-inch and 8-inch wafers, targeting 1.6T bandwidth and beyond for AI data center connectivity.
key_facts.excerpt: UMC, HyperLight, and UMC's subsidiary Wavetek announced a strategic collaboration to mass-produce HyperLight's TFLN chiplet platform on 6-inch and 8-inch wafers, targeting 1.6T bandwidth and beyond.

key_facts.fact: The TFLN platform enables extreme high modulation bandwidth, CMOS-level drive voltage, and ultralow optical loss, reducing laser consumption and supporting CMOS direct-drive for lower power consumption. Applications include short-reach data center pluggables, coherent datacom/telecom modules, and co-packaged optics (CPO).
key_facts.excerpt: The platform enables extreme high modulation bandwidth, CMOS-level drive voltage and ultralow optical loss, reducing laser consumption and supporting CMOS direct-drive voltage for lower power consumption.

key_facts.fact: Wavetek previously scaled TFLN from lab to a 6-inch production line, while UMC adds 8-inch wafer expertise for AI infrastructure scale. UMC is simultaneously pursuing silicon photonics through a 2025 licensing agreement with imec for the iSiPP300 process.
key_facts.excerpt: Wavetek previously scaled TFLN from lab to a 6-inch production line. UMC adds 8-inch expertise for AI infrastructure scale.

stories.headline: Robinson Helicopter launches Robinson Unmanned unit, merging crewed and uncrewed aircraft

key_facts.fact: Robinson Helicopter Company launched Robinson Unmanned, a new business unit consolidating Ascent Aerosystems (small UAS developer) with Robinson's larger uncrewed platforms based on its R44 and R66 helicopters.
key_facts.excerpt: Robinson Unmanned consolidates two operations: Ascent Aerosystems (an existing small UAS developer) merged with Robinson Helicopter's larger uncrewed platforms derived from crewed aircraft models.

key_facts.fact: The unit covers Group 1-2 small UAS (Helius and Spirit co-axial platforms from Ascent) through Group 3-4 larger systems (uncrewed versions of Robinson R44 and R66 helicopters), integrating Sikorsky's Matrix autonomy system on the R66 Turbine platform.
key_facts.excerpt: Small systems (Group 1 & 2): Helius and Spirit co-axial platforms from Ascent. Larger systems (Group 3 & 4): Uncrewed versions based on Robinson's R44 and R66 helicopters. Integration with Sikorsky's Matrix system represents a significant technical collaboration.

key_facts.fact: The new entity targets both defense and commercial markets, reflecting Robinson's strategic shift toward scalable autonomous aircraft development rather than maintaining separate product lines.
key_facts.excerpt: The new entity incorporates crewed and uncrewed capabilities to tackle a variety of mission demands in both defence and commercial markets.

sources.title: Robinson launches new uncrewed aircraft business unit, unveils new UAS cargo platform
